messages.content: Implement a Python function from a JSON behavioral card. The card is the only task specification. Return a JSON object with a single string field code containing executable Python source. Define solve with the card's exact signature. Use only Python's standard library. Allowed imports: math, itertools, functools, collections, heapq, bisect, statistics, fractions, operator, typing. Do not import or call NumPy, SymPy, NetworkX or any other third-party library. Do not read files, use network, introspection, eval, exec, input or print. Implement computations yourself using built-ins and the allowed standard library. Return plain JSON-compatible values, not iterators or sets; use string keys in dictionaries. Include any helper functions in the code. No tests or main block. Raise ValueError where the card requires it.

Implement this card:
{
  "algorithm": [
    "For each element in the input lists x and y, compute the remainder using the formula: remainder = x % y",
    "If x and y are scalars, return a single integer result.",
    "If x and y are lists of the same length or broadcastable to the same length, return a list of remainders with the same length as the input lists.",
    "The result has the same sign as the divisor y (not the dividend x)."
  ],
  "constraints": [
    "Values and results fit within signed int64",
    "Divisors y must be nonzero",
    "No broadcasting beyond 1D lists is supported",
    "The remainder has the same sign as the divisor y",
    "The function does not support IEEE remainder or floor division remainder"
  ],
  "edge_cases": [
    "When y is 0, return 0 (as per the contract, divisors are nonzero, but the documentation states this behavior for completeness)",
    "Empty lists: return an empty list",
    "When x and y are both integers, return a single integer",
    "When x is a scalar and y is a list, or vice versa, broadcast the scalar to match the list length",
    "When x and y are lists of different lengths but broadcastable (e.g., 1D lists with compatible shapes), return the remainder for each element after broadcasting"
  ],
  "inputs": "x and y are integers or 1-D lists of integers. Support scalar/scalar, scalar/list, list/scalar and lists of the same length (including empty).",
  "method_id": "numpy.remainder",
  "output": "A list of integers with the same length as the input lists (or a single integer if both inputs are scalars). The remainder has the same sign as the divisor y.",
  "purpose": "Compute the element-wise remainder of division with the same sign as the divisor",
  "signature": "solve(x, y)"
}
